title: I kept losing links to AI-built games, so I made an arcade. It now has nearly 2,000 games.
author: mr_pr
selftext:
Hi everyone, I’m Rich, and I’ve been building Playground Arcade.

This started because I kept seeing games people had made with AI, thinking “I want to try that”, then losing the link and struggling to find the game or its creator again.

So I built somewhere to bring them together: [playgroundarcade.com](https://playgroundarcade.com/).

There are now just shy of 2,000 games and counting, covering everything from racing and platformers to card battles, RPGs and multiplayer experiments.

As the library grows, I’m putting more work into discovery, and helping people find something they actually want to play: 'try these three' randomisation, short gameplay previews where available, device filters, play counts, ratings, written reviews and personalised suggestions for both guests and people that sign in 

(There's an EXP system that levels players up based on game plays, ratings and written reviews, because why not gamify discovery and giving creators feedback!).

I know many in here are building games - so, any thoughts on how to help people better find your games, I'm all ears. 

There've been a few thousand game plays across more than a third of the games onsite since launching, which is awesome, and means people are finding games they love.

Every listing credits the creator and links to the original game. Playground doesn’t rehost people’s games. Browsing is free, you don’t need an account, and creators can submit their games for free too (more than 50 have, which is really promising!).

I grew up hiding Newgrounds and Bored tabs during school IT lessons, so building this has been a lot of fun - and made even better when Bored featured it last week! 

If you’ve made a game with AI assistance, I’d love to see it. And I’m interested in any/all feedback: what would make a directory like this more useful to you?

comments.author: linguaarush_dev
comments.body:
Great initiative, Rich.   
  
One thought from a fellow creator: the core issue isn't just *listing* games, it's actively finding players who will actually play them.

I’ve also built a few JavaScript-based games. My first was a fast translation game that I still maintain, and I also found a school that will host the game on their server.  
More recently, I created a crazy political satire game that is currently booming (mostly through organic niche sharing). It is also available on reddit games. 

Even with that success, sustainable discovery is tough.   
  
To answer your question on what would make a directory more useful:   
a) it would be great to see features that actively match player *intent* or *mood* to a game, or ways to highlight games that are looking for specific types of feedback.   
  
b) Gamifying discovery is a clever start, but bridging the gap between 'browsing a list' and 'finding a player base' is the real holy grail for creators like us.

How do you think the Playground Arcade will tackle that?

replies.author: mr_pr
replies.body:
100% agree. Being listed doesn't mean being found.

That's what I mean about now really focusing on discovery, and it's why I'm bringing new things to this every day. 

Gameplay previews, games being recommended for you based on your gameplay (that's the 'Your Playground' tab at the top, and that's for guests (unless they clear cache) and, better yet, people that sign up so it saves all info), creator pages (so discovering one game from somebody can lead to others by the same creator) - plus your usual written reviews and ratings. 

I'm looking at a weekly personalised email to those that are signed up as well - 'hey, you played this game, rated this one, wrote a review for this one - here are a few suggestions we think you'd love'.

The challenge now (hence sharing here!) is bringing more players into that mix and understanding what gets them opening games and coming back.

Mood is really interesting - do you mean like, instead of genre, it could be: 'I'm after a quick play', 'I'm in the mood for a game that'll challenge me' - that sort of thing?

Also, specific creator feedback - great shout. I don't know how I pull that into the site yet, but I'll have a think.

Still early days, but helping people find something they actually want to play is exactly where I want to take this. And please do share your games - I’d love to have a look and have them onsite!

comments.author: mr_pr
comments.body:
Also - I've seen people talk about lack of numbers transparency on game directories in other threads. 

You'll see every play, rating and review on Playground is real. I'm very, very happy sharing stats - mostly because... why not? I want creators to know it might well bring them new players.

I'm doing this for fun, and to shine a light on what creators are doing. This isn't my full-time thing, I just get weirdly obsessed with building fun things that celebrate great work (I did the same with a site called PRexamples celebrating great PR and marketing stunts/campaigns - sold it after it had become the UK's best-read PR site, it's now called Famous Campaigns and is awesome if you're into that sort of thing).

Started building Playground a month ago. I'd say I went 'public'/launched when I shared it on Hacker News exactly 7 days ago. 

From there, Bored featured it in their arcade portals section, which brought \~500 uniques a day for a couple of days until they unceremoniously removed it - I'm genuinely gutted, I played on Bored all the time as a kid!

**Anyway, sorry to ramble - numbers here:**

|Measure|Total|
|:-|:-|
|Recorded game opens|**3,369**|
|Different games opened|**642**|
|Ratings|**95**, across 77 games|
|Written reviews|**16**, included within those ratings (and, I make up about half of those)|
|Website visits, last 30 days|**4,030**|

Looking at those browsers that opened at least one game:

|Different games opened|Browsers|Share|
|:-|:-|:-|
|**2 or more**|612|**43%**|
|**3 or more**|340|**24%**|
|**5 or more**|136|**10%**|

The average is **2.33 different games per recorded browser**.

I've just added a new feature, publishing soon - every game tile will recommend three similar games, alongside 'Your Playground' suggesting games you'd like, too (irrelevent of plays/reviews).

I'll be using these %s as a benchmark to improve on. To see 10% of visitors playing 5 or more is pretty cool.
